51fa3fcc-9d5f-52f0-809d-62d7cdd8a865.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.

e686bd4d-3ebd-5e55-ba39-f26971247965.content: Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.

019662a9-6f03-527f-9b6d-be5a2966d9e9.content: The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.

a6dfe9a7-1df8-561f-8d3e-fc19518beca9.content: A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.

7047a23d-45b3-5d5c-a00b-c12552e9680d.content: HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.

50a71968-7e3f-5b99-b3fa-769af386d0c0.content: Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.

ae1610f6-a855-56c1-a0fb-fd3207dab615.content: Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.

d2825b84-b4a6-58c9-8f8e-9e19c6192a03.content: This advisor has repeatedly seen reviewers inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
